literature_register.citation: Malerbo-Souza DT. 2011. The corn pollen as a food source for honeybees. Acta Scientiarum Agronomy 33(4).

literature_register.citation: Embrapa Milho e Sorgo. Flutuacao populacional de Dalbulus maidis em milho, safrinha 2022.
literature_register.finding: Yellow sticky traps in three areas from March to June 2022 recorded a population peak at maize stage V8 (162 adults on 25 April) in one trap and at V7 (16 May) in another, with no correlation found to phenological stage, temperature or precipitation.
literature_register.limitations: Not opened. Minas Gerais, not Parana. Single season, three areas. The authors themselves report no correlation with phenology, which weakens any phenological generalisation.

literature_register.finding: 68 traps were installed before safrinha sowing and changed weekly to the reproductive stage; a dilution effect was observed as insects concentrated near summer maize then dispersed into the larger safrinha area.

literature_register.citation: Meneses AR, Silva NNP da, Querino RB, Oliveira CM. 2015. Ocorrencia e flutuacao populacional de parasitoides de Dalbulus maidis (DeLong & Wolcott) (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) em milho. In: 14 Simposio de Controle Biologico (SICONBIOL), 14-18 June 2015, Teresopolis, RJ. Londrina: Sociedade Entomologica do Brasil.
literature_register.finding: Weekly collections using sentinel plants bearing D. maidis eggs on their leaves identified three species: A. breviphragma, P. subflava and P. longifrangiata. The authors state these are the FIRST RECORDS of P. subflava and P. longifrangiata parasitising D. maidis eggs in Brazil, and the first record of the A. breviphragma association with the corn leafhopper in the Brazilian Northeast.
literature_register.host_or_prey_relationship: Egg parasitoids attacking D. maidis eggs on sentinel plants
literature_register.limitations: Conference abstract, so no parasitism rates, no replication detail, no identification keys and no statistical treatment are reported. One experimental site in Piaui over 15 months. Species identifications are not independently verifiable from the abstract. The PDF renders the genus as Paracentobia, a typographic error for Paracentrobia.
literature_register.location: Maize crops in the Embrapa Meio-Norte experimental area, Teresina, Piaui, Brazil; February 2013 to May 2014
literature_register.organism: Anagrus breviphragma Soyka (Mymaridae), Paracentrobia subflava (Girault) and Pseudoligosita longifrangiata (Viggiani) (Trichogrammatidae)

resource_landscape.known_limitations: Unannotated, so locus-level promotion from this resource is not available under F.1/H.4 without external annotation. Not an NTO; listed for context and for taxid resolution only, so no assessability is assigned.

resource_landscape.resource_notes: GITV01 is the transcriptome background already used by NB01-NB03 (e.g. GITV01012450.1, GITV01008430.1) and the only one pinned in data/reference/manifest.json, confirming continuity with the upstream stages. resource_landscape.known_limitations: No transcript resource was detected in the sources queried: 0 mRNA records, 0 RefSeq RNA, 0 TSA. Genome is unannotated. GENOME_TIER evidence only, and GENOME_HOMOLOGY != TRANSCRIPT_TARGET_EVIDENCE (F.2).
resource_landscape.resource_notes: Chromosome-level, released 2025-10-26, same Tree of Life programme as the D. maidis assembly. Second haplotype GCA_976225295.1 (scaffold) also detected.

resource_landscape.known_limitations: Transcript-tier coverage gap for the closest phylogenetic non-target currently proposed. Absence of detection in the sources queried is not evidence of global absence.
resource_landscape.resource_notes: No transcript-tier resource was detected in the metadata sources queried. 3 SRA entries were reported, but raw reads are not a usable screening resource and assembling them is derived work outside L9a and outside NB04 scope as planned.

resource_landscape.known_limitations: No resource detected in the sources queried. Receptor remains in the ecological panel at its tier under D.5; only assessability is affected. Absence of detection is not evidence of global absence.
resource_landscape.resource_notes: Taxid resolves, but zero nucleotide records, zero assemblies and zero TSA were detected in the sources queried. One SRA entry was reported.

resource_landscape.known_limitations: Whether this is a PHYLOGENETIC_PROXY or a SURROGATE_RESOURCE is a D.4 decision, not an L9a one, and L9a does not select it. A surrogate never closes the original receptor's coverage gap and a no-hit in it is never a no-hit in A. albidula. TSA limitations per F.1.
resource_landscape.resource_notes: The only congeneric transcriptome detected for genus Agallia in the sources queried. If adopted, would require surrogate_for_organism_id under D.4.

resource_landscape.known_limitations: Largest arthropod resource detected in the candidate set (2.3 Gb), which places it at one extreme of the size span relevant to DATABASE_SIZE_DEPENDENT_REPORTING_BEHAVIOR (G.5).
resource_landscape.resource_notes: Chromosome-level RefSeq with an NCBI annotation release. The best-resourced Cicadellidae detected in this sweep; among the 61 Cicadellidae assemblies reported, this was also the best assembly returned at family rank.

resource_landscape.known_limitations: Phylogenetically distant from Dalbulus within Cicadellidae; a PHYLOGENETIC_PROXY role must not be conflated with a SURROGATE_RESOURCE role (D.4), and L9a assigns neither. Total bases inferred from a sample.

resource_landscape.resource_notes: No other Mymaridae assembly was detected in the sources queried, and this is the only congeneric resource detected for Anagrus. Contig level, unannotated.

resource_landscape.known_limitations: Family rank only, not congeneric with Paracentrobia or Pseudoligosita. A proxy at family rank would not close either genus coverage gap (D.4), and L9a selects no proxy. Total bases inferred from a sample.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None. The program is fixed by the modality: CP3 is nucleotide local alignment against nucleotide subjects.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Choosing a program whose seeding model cannot recover short divergent local alignments.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Fixed by architecture, declared in the G0 policy as the modality definition. Not a calibrated value.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..parameter: program selection (blastn vs megablast vs dc-megablast)

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does the task's default seeding and extension recover the planted-alignment matrix at each size class, in particular the short high-identity and the longer lower-identity cases?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: blastn-short alters defaults for word_size, evalue and penalties as a bundle; silently inheriting a different bundle would invalidate every other calibrated value.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Task is a bundle, not a scalar. Changing it invalidates P03-P08 jointly and triggers RECALIBRATION_REQUIRED.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..truncation_relevance: INDIRECT. Task changes defaults that affect how many alignments qualify.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: What is the smallest planted alignment length, at each identity level, that this word size recovers on the declared fixtures, per size class?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: design space to be declared pre-G1 as a set of candidate values; no value selected here
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: A word size too large silently loses short or divergent alignments; the loss is invisible because no alignment is emitted to inspect.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: The NB02/NB03 value 11 was justified for a handful-of-transcripts database. Its recovery behaviour at 50-2300 Mb is uncharacterised. PRECEDENT_ONLY.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: At a fixed alignment score, does a single configured limit produce comparable reporting behaviour across the three size classes, and which planted alignments fall outside reporting at each class?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: design space to be declared pre-G1; no value selected here
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..database_size_relevance: HIGH. This is the primary locus of DATABASE_SIZE_DEPENDENT_REPORTING_BEHAVIOR.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: A fixed limit makes the minimum reportable score depend on effective search space, so the same planted alignment can be reported in a small resource and unreported in a large one.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Never a biological acceptability cutoff and never a ranking criterion (PLAN G.5). PRECEDENT_ONLY.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..truncation_relevance: HIGH. Unreported is indistinguishable from absent unless calibrated.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does the default reward/penalty ratio recover the moderate-identity planted alignments, or does it favour only high-identity ungapped cases?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: default; or an explicit declared pair with P06
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..current_precedent: BLAST default for task (NOT_SET in NB02/NB03)
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: An unstated default is a hidden parameter: it is part of the executed configuration but absent from the declared one, so DECLARED == EXECUTED cannot be verified.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Must be recorded explicitly even if the default is kept. K.4f forbids omitting a non-applicable or defaulted field.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Same as P05; reward and penalty are calibrated as a pair, never independently.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: default; or an explicit declared pair with P05
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..current_precedent: BLAST default for task (NOT_SET in NB02/NB03)
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Mismatched reward/penalty ratio shifts the identity at which alignments stop scoring above threshold.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: The ratio, not either value alone, determines the identity sensitivity.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does the configuration recover the gapped planted alignments at each gap pattern in the matrix?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..current_precedent: BLAST default for task (NOT_SET in NB02/NB03)
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Gap penalties too severe reduce gapped recovery to zero while ungapped recovery looks healthy, producing a modality-specific blind spot.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: CP3 is the only NB04 modality that can recover gapped alignments at all; CP2 excludes indels by FORMAL_SPACE_SCOPE_LIMITATION.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Same as P07; calibrated jointly with gapopen.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..current_precedent: BLAST default for task (NOT_SET in NB02/NB03)
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: As P07.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Calibrated as a pair with P07.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does disabling DUST change recovery on the repeat-context fixtures, and how many additional reported HSPs does it produce per size class?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..current_precedent: no (PRECEDENT_ONLY; PLAN G.4 retains -dust no as a stated preference)
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: With dust on, low-complexity-driven alignments are silently removed, which is a masked false absence. With dust off, repeat-driven HSP counts can inflate and interact with output caps.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: PLAN G.4 already states the preference: keep matches visible and labelled rather than silently masked, with a dustmasker-derived low_complexity_overlap_fraction per HSP. Calibration characterises the cost, it does not reopen the preference.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..truncation_relevance: MEDIUM. Disabling masking raises HSP volume and therefore cap pressure.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: With -dust no, is soft_masking inert, or does it still affect seeding on the repeat fixtures?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: An unstated interaction between dust and soft_masking could reintroduce masking that the project believes it disabled.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Interaction with P09 must be verified on fixtures, not assumed.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None, if the normalized subject representation is uppercase throughout.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Lower-case residues in an acquired FASTA would become masked regions, producing a resource-specific silent blind spot.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Depends on the CP1 normalization contract. A QA check on the normalized FASTA is cheaper than calibrating this.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..truncation_relevance: MEDIUM if a resource arrives mixed-case

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None. Both strands are required by C-3 and the PLAN G.2b orientation contract.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Searching one strand would make every minus-strand correspondence a false absence.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Reusable from precedent as an architectural requirement, not as a calibrated value.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: For each size class and record architecture, can the configuration be shown not to lose qualifying subjects, by order invariance and partition recovery rather than by the parameter value? And what value does the PINNED build actually report as its default?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: an explicitly declared value PLUS an empirical invariance demonstration. Omitting the flag is NOT a no-cap option: it selects the engine default
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..current_precedent: 100000, justified in NB02 C17 as larger than the database so no subject is dropped (PRECEDENT_ONLY). The BLAST+ ENGINE DEFAULT is 500, not unlimited
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..database_size_relevance: INDIRECT. Risk scales with RECORD COUNT, not with total bases.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..determinism_relevance: HIGH. Order dependence is itself a determinism failure.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Shah et al. 2019 demonstrated strong database-order dependence in historical BLAST+ versions, where a better alignment could be missed because a weaker subject appeared earlier. Contemporary BLAST+ documentation still records order dependence, at minimum for tie-breaking among equally scoring subjects. NB04 does not presume that the installed version is free of truncation or order effects, and does not presume the 2018 behaviour persists unchanged; it tests invariance empirically regardless of version.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: The NB02/NB03 justification was structural: 100000 exceeded a database of a handful of transcripts. That argument does NOT transfer to NB04, where a transcript resource can hold 20000-60000 records. PRECEDENT_ONLY and not inherited. CORRECTED IN V2: the engine default is documented as 500 and ties are documented as broken by database order, so leaving the flag unset would be MORE restrictive than the precedent, not less. The effective value must appear in the configuration artifact even when not passed on the command line, or DECLARED == EXECUTED is unverifiable. The authoritative value is whatever the pinned build reports via blastn -help, recorded at calibration time; PROVENANCE UPGRADED AT THE SECOND AUDIT: the default of 500, the keep-semantics and the tie-breaking-by-database-order statement were verified by the independent auditor directly against current NCBI documentation, and NCBI release notes were verified to confirm that BLAST+ 2.8.1 disabled the aggressive optimisation behind the Shah et al. behaviour. The authoritative value for a given run remains whatever the pinned build reports via blastn -help, recorded at calibration time
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..truncation_relevance: CRITICAL. This is the central truncation parameter.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: On the multiple-HSPs-per-subject and duplicated-target fixtures, does the configuration report every qualifying HSP, and is per-subject HSP count ever observed at a ceiling?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: unset (preferred); or a declared value with an invariance demonstration
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: A per-subject HSP cap discards alignments within a retained subject. The subject is present in the output, so the loss is harder to detect than a dropped subject.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Leaving it unset is the precedent and the preferred design, but unset must still be demonstrated against a fixture that would saturate a cap. CONFIRMED IN V2 AND VERIFIED AGAINST CURRENT NCBI DOCUMENTATION AT THE SECOND AUDIT: BLAST+ documentation states that when max_hsps is not set, all HSPs meeting the E-value criterion are kept, so unlike max_target_seqs there is no hidden numeric default here and the NB02/NB03 precedent is correctly formulated. The effective state must still be recorded explicitly in the configuration artifact

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None, if excluded. If ever set, it would need a calibration question of its own.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: A percent-identity filter is the parameter most likely to be mistaken for a biological threshold. It would also discard the moderate-identity and long-lower-identity planted cases by construction.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Recommended excluded. Identity is a descriptor computed after the fact (PLAN G.8), never a search filter.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None, if excluded.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: A query-coverage filter would discard short planted alignments by construction, which is exactly the class the k16 sensitivity question cares about elsewhere in the project.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Recommended excluded for the same reason as P15.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None, if excluded.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Culling removes HSPs enveloped by higher-scoring ones. For an occurrence-complete contract this is silent loss of real alignments.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Recommended excluded. Incompatible with the PLAN G.8 requirement that all canonical CP3 aggregates derive from a complete HSP table.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None, if excluded.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Best-hit filtering discards subjects judged redundant, which removes the very multiplicity the evidence model records.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Recommended excluded.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None, if excluded.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: As P18.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Recommended excluded.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None, if excluded.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Keeps only the best HSP region per subject, discarding the rest.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Recommended excluded.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Do the default extension dropoffs truncate the longer lower-identity planted alignments, splitting one planted alignment into several reported HSPs or losing its ends?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Extension dropoff can shorten a reported alignment relative to the planted one, which corrupts coordinate and length QA without failing any obvious check.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Directly implicated in QA criterion B (coordinate correctness) on the long lower-identity fixture.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does the two-hit requirement affect recovery of short high-identity alignments at the declared word size?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: A two-hit seeding requirement can make short alignments undetectable regardless of their identity.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Interacts with P03; calibrate the pair on the short-alignment fixtures.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Would fixing the effective search space make reporting behaviour comparable across size classes, and what does it cost in interpretability of the reported E-values?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: NOT_SET in production (preferred); SANCTIONED AS A QA-ONLY NORMALIZATION TECHNIQUE for QA-F2, where the effective search space must be held constant across partitionings for a set-equality comparison to be meaningful
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..database_size_relevance: CRITICAL. This is the only parameter that directly manipulates effective search space.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Fixing dbsize makes E-values no longer describe the resource actually searched, so an E-value in the output would not mean what a reader assumes.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Raised because it is the one direct lever on DATABASE_SIZE_DEPENDENT_REPORTING_BEHAVIOR. Still NOT recommended for production: fixing dbsize would make a reported E-value stop describing the resource actually searched. CORRECTED IN V2: it IS now sanctioned for the QA-F2 fixture comparison only, because without normalizing effective search space a set-equality test between a full database and its shards is not mathematically valid. Using it in QA does not license using it in production
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..truncation_relevance: MEDIUM. It is a candidate lever for the size-dependence problem.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: None, if excluded.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Would make every gapped planted alignment unrecoverable.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Recommended excluded.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does sum statistics change the E-value assigned to the multiple-HSP fixtures relative to single-HSP treatment?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Sum statistics couple the E-value of one HSP to the presence of others on the same subject, so an E-value becomes non-local and the monotonicity QA criterion can fail for a non-defect reason.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Directly implicated in QA criterion H. Must be recorded before interpreting any score/E-value monotonicity result.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does the field set carry everything PLAN G.8 requires per HSP, including BTOP, qlen, slen, gap bases and gap opens separately, and the fields needed to reconstruct the alignment?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: the NB01-NB03 field set, extended with the fields PLAN G.8 requires
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..current_precedent: outfmt 6 with qseqid sseqid pident length qlen slen qstart qend sstart send sstrand evalue bitscore mismatch gapopen gaps qcovs btop (NB01-NB03)
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..determinism_relevance: HIGH. Field order and formatting determine byte-level output determinism.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: A missing field makes an HSP non-reconstructible, so the row cannot support the absence or presence statement built on it.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: The strongest reuse candidate from NB01-NB03. BTOP is already parsed and validated by a regex in nb03_specificity.py and is what PLAN G.8 alignment reconstruction depends on.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..truncation_relevance: MEDIUM. The field set must be able to EXPRESS a saturation signal, e.g. per-subject HSP counts.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does thread count change the reported result set or its order at any size class?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: 1 (preferred); or >1 with a demonstrated determinism invariance
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..database_size_relevance: MEDIUM. Large classes are where single-threaded cost becomes a real constraint.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Multi-threading can alter database traversal and therefore, given P13's order dependence, alter which subjects are retained. It can also change output ordering, breaking byte-level determinism.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: The tension is explicit: determinism argues for 1, the LARGE size class argues for more. If cost forces >1, that is a RESOURCE_CONSTRAINT with a determinism demonstration attached, never a biological justification.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does -parse_seqids change identifier handling in a way that affects record identity or record count as BLAST sees it?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..current_precedent: dbtype nucl, parse_seqids used in NB01, title set, out set (PRECEDENT_ONLY)
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Identifier mangling breaks the join from HSP rows back to the resource registry, which breaks provenance rather than detection.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: NB01 precedent. The database build is part of the configuration and must be hashed (NB03 already hashes the database binaries).

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does a multi-volume database change the result set relative to a single-volume database of the same content, at the same configuration?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: declared explicitly; volume count recorded per resource
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..database_size_relevance: CRITICAL. Only the MEDIUM and LARGE classes produce multi-volume databases.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: BLAST scans volumes in sequence. Given P13's order dependence, volume structure is a form of record ordering, so volume count is a potential truncation variable that the NB02/NB03 precedent never had to consider.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Newly relevant at NB04 scale and absent from all project precedent. Central to the partition-invariance QA criterion.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..truncation_relevance: CRITICAL. Database partitioning is both a truncation RISK and the proposed truncation REMEDY.

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Is the input record order fixed and hashed, so that the order-invariance test has a defined baseline to vary against?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: a declared canonical record order, hashed
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: Without a declared baseline order, an order-invariance result is not reproducible and the truncation demonstration cannot be re-verified.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Not a BLAST flag. It is the precondition that makes QA criteria E and F meaningful.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..parameter: deterministic record ordering of the input FASTA

08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..calibration_question: Does the parser reject a truncated, malformed or partially written table rather than silently yielding fewer rows?
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..candidate_design_space: reuse, with an added saturation and completeness check
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..failure_mode: A truncated output file parsed without error is the worst failure mode available: it looks like a complete result with fewer hits.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..notes: Strong reuse candidate, but it must be extended: the NB02/NB03 parser was never asked to detect output truncation because the databases could not produce it.
08_b4_calibration_parameter_matrix_v2_1..parameter: HSP table parser and BTOP validation

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: every MUST_BE_REPORTED planted alignment is present. Cases classified CHARACTERIZED_NOT_ASSERTED are recorded with their outcome and are NOT scored pass or fail
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: A missing MUST_BE_REPORTED alignment means the configuration cannot recover a correspondence that exists by construction. It is a detection defect of the configuration, never a statement about biology
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.fixture_dependency: F01, F02, F04, F05, F06, F07; planted cases PC01, PC02, PC07, PC08, PC09, PC11, PC12
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: count of planted alignments classified MUST_BE_REPORTED that appear in the parsed HSP table, per fixture and per planted case

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: exact agreement for PC01. For PC02 and PC06 agreement within the tolerance declared in advance for that case, with the tolerance justified by extension dropoff
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: Coordinate error invalidates every downstream aggregate that depends on position: covered_nt, the union, locus mapping and the 1253/1254 contrast. A tolerance stated only after seeing the result is not a tolerance
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: reported qstart, qend, sstart, send compared against planted coordinates, 1-based inclusive, with a declared numerical tolerance per planted case

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: minus-strand planted alignments report sstrand minus and their coordinates invert back to the planted interval exactly
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: A strand or coordinate-convention error silently mislocates every minus-strand correspondence. Required by C-3 and the PLAN G.2b orientation contract
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: sstrand value and whether subject coordinates map back to the planted interval under the declared coordinate convention

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: byte-identical output across runs, with volatile metadata excluded from the hashed set as the project already does for execution_metadata.json
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: Non-determinism means no hash can certify the result and no gate certification can be bound to it (PLAN J.1)
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: SHA256 of the parsed and canonically serialised HSP table across repeated runs of the identical command on the identical database

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: identical result SETS across record orders. Row order may differ and is normalised before comparison
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: Shah et al. 2019 demonstrated strong database-order dependence in historical BLAST+ versions, where a better alignment could be missed because a weaker subject appeared earlier. Contemporary BLAST+ documentation still records order dependence, at minimum for tie-breaking among equally scoring subjects. NB04 does not presume that the installed version is free of truncation or order effects, and does not presume the 2018 behaviour persists unchanged; it tests invariance empirically regardless of version. Failure means the result depends on an arbitrary property of the input file, and no absence statement may be made from it.
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.fixture_dependency: F02, F06; PC13 primarily, PC07 and PC11 secondarily
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: set equality of reported (subject_id, qstart, qend, sstart, send, strand) tuples between a run on the declared canonical record order and runs on at least one declared permuted record order

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: every MUST_BE_REPORTED planted alignment is recovered in BOTH the integral database and the sharded union. No set equality is required
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: A planted alignment present in the sharded union but absent from the integral run is direct evidence of loss in the single pass, which is the truncation signal this criterion exists to detect. The converse, present in the integral run and absent from a shard, indicates a sharding or harness defect
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.fixture_dependency: F02, F06; planted cases classified MUST_BE_REPORTED
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: presence of each MUST_BE_REPORTED planted alignment in the single-database result set, and in the union of the shard result sets, under the identical configuration

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: identical result sets once effective search space is held constant. Without that normalization no equality is expected and none is required
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: SPLIT FROM QA-F IN V2 BECAUSE THE ORIGINAL WAS NOT MATHEMATICALLY VALID. Partitioning changes effective search space, so under one fixed E-value cutoff a marginal alignment can be unreported in the full database and reported in a smaller shard with no truncation whatever. The E-value decides whether the tuple enters the output at all, so comparing tuples while ignoring the E-value difference does not rescue the test: a correct BLAST configuration would fail it by construction. Equality is therefore demanded only under normalization, achieved for QA purposes by fixing the effective search space (-dbsize or -searchsp) across partitionings, or by re-evaluating shard candidates with integral-database statistics. This is a QA-fixture technique and does NOT license using -dbsize in production. A failure under normalization is genuine evidence of loss
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: set equality of reported alignment tuples between the integral database and the sharded union, computed ONLY under a declared normalization of effective search space, or after explicit re-evaluation of shard candidates against the integral-database statistics

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: no saturation indicator is at its ceiling, AND QA-E and QA-F1 both hold, AND QA-F2 holds under its declared normalization. A parameter value alone never satisfies this criterion, and an unset flag is not an absent ceiling
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: Saturation at a ceiling, or failure of QA-E, QA-F1 or normalized QA-F2, yields OUTPUT_TRUNCATED or TRUNCATION_UNRESOLVED. Under NO_ABSENCE_STATEMENT_WITH_UNRESOLVED_TRUNCATION_RISK neither state permits an absence statement for the affected scope
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.fixture_dependency: F02, F03, F06; PC12 and PC13
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: saturation indicators: reported distinct subject count compared against the EFFECTIVE max_target_seqs, which is the engine default of 500 where the flag is not passed; maximum per-subject HSP count compared against any configured max_hsps; presence of any engine warning on stderr

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: for a fixed planted alignment, bit score is expected to be stable across classes while the E-value rises with effective search space, so the minimum reportable score rises with resource size. The relationship is RECORDED, not asserted in advance
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: A deviation from monotonic E-value behaviour in effective search space indicates either a sum-statistics interaction (P25) or a configuration difference between runs, and must be resolved before the series is interpreted. No proportional sensitivity ratio is derived from the size ratio
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.fixture_dependency: F02, F04, F05; the identical PC03 and PC06 instances planted in all three
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: for one identical planted alignment: raw alignment score, bit score, E-value, effective search space as reported by the engine, resource total bases, record count, and whether the alignment was reported

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: the parser accepts the valid table and RAISES on each malformed or truncated input. It never silently yields fewer rows
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: A truncated output file parsed without error is the most dangerous failure mode in the whole design: it presents as a complete result with fewer hits. The NB01/NB03 parser and its BTOP regex were never required to detect this, because those databases could not produce it
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.fixture_dependency: F01, F02, plus deliberately corrupted copies of a valid output
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: parser outcome on a valid table, a truncated table, a table with a malformed BTOP, and a table with an illegal character

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: Distinguished from QA-D in scope only: QA-D is within-session, QA-J spans invocations. Failure indicates environment or state dependence not captured in the declared configuration
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: as QA-D, extended across separate process invocations and, where applicable, separate sessions on the declared environment

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: every field present and explicit. A non-applicable field says so explicitly rather than being omitted
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: An incomplete provenance record makes DECLARED == EXECUTED unverifiable and makes the calibration non-reusable, which is a G1 certification failure under PLAN K.4f and K.4g
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: presence and non-null status of every field the configuration and calibration artifacts require: tool, tool_version, database-format version, OS and environment, full command line, configuration hash, every fixture hash, database binary hashes, resource size class, UTC date

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: every resource actually screened falls inside a calibrated envelope on BOTH the total-bases axis and the record-count axis
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: A resource outside the envelope on either axis yields RECALIBRATION_REQUIRED for that resource. It does not invalidate the calibration for resources that are inside
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: for each real resource selected at CP1: measured total bases and record count mapped against the calibrated class envelopes, on both axes

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: exact match, including defaulted parameters recorded explicitly
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: A divergence means the certified configuration artifact does not describe the run, so no result from that run can be attributed to it. Required by PLAN J.2 CP3 and K.4f
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: the reconstructed command line derived from the configuration artifact compared against the command line actually executed and logged

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: no reported HSP is attributed to a planted sentinel. Background HSPs may legitimately be present and are characterised per size class rather than required to be absent
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: CORRECTED IN V2. The earlier formulation required zero reported HSPs, which was wrong: chance local correspondences in a synthetic background are expected, and more so at hundreds of Mb to Gb, because an E-value expresses how many matches of a given score arise by chance in a database of that size. The real failure is the pipeline attributing a hit to a sentinel that was never planted, or background volume so high that it indicates a configuration far more permissive than intended
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: on the PC14 no-planted-alignment background: whether any reported HSP corresponds to a planted sentinel that does not exist, plus the distribution of background HSP count, score and E-value per size class

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: the outcome per gap pattern is recorded. No prior pass or fail expectation is set, because gapped recovery is a heuristic property being measured
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: Zero recovery across every gap pattern would mean the configuration is effectively ungapped, which must be recorded as a SEARCH_RECOVERY_LIMITATION and disclosed on every CP3 absence statement rather than left implicit
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: for each declared gap pattern: reported or not, and if reported, the gap positions reconstructed from BTOP, with query-side and subject-side gaps counted separately

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: the two sets are disjoint. Every row of the calibration artifact carries fixture_role of TUNING or VALIDATION, and the selected configuration has at least one VALIDATION row with selection_outcome SELECTED and a stated selection_reason
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: Selecting and validating on the same fixtures makes the recovery characterisation circular, so the resulting claim describes the fixtures rather than the configuration. Required by PLAN G.7c and L-34g
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: set intersection of the fixture and planted-case identifiers used to SELECT the configuration and those used to VALIDATE it

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: identical result sets. If output hashes differ only in row order, that is recorded and the canonical sort is applied before hashing
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: Given the record-order dependence established by QA-E, multi-threaded database traversal is a plausible route to a differing result set. If invariance fails, thread count is pinned at the declared value as a determinism requirement and any cost consequence is a RESOURCE_CONSTRAINT, never a biological justification
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: result-set equality and output hash across the declared thread count and at least one alternative

09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.expected_behavior: recorded per fixture and per size class. No threshold is set and no configuration is rejected on these figures
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.failure_interpretation: Performance is technical characterisation only. If cost makes integral execution infeasible, that is recorded as RESOURCE_SEARCH_BUDGET_EXCEEDED and handled as a RESOURCE_CONSTRAINT with an amendment, never as a biological justification for narrowing the search
09_b4_calibration_qa_matrix_v2.tsv.metric: wall time, CPU time, peak memory, database size, record count, query count, reported HSP count, reported subject count

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM, Oliveira E, Souza IRP, Alves E, Dolezal W, Paradell S, Remes Lenicov AMM, Frizzas MR. 2013. Abundance and species richness of leafhoppers and planthoppers (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae and Delphacidae) in Brazilian maize crops. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Sweep-net sampling 2005-2007, 198 samples, recovered 4233 Cicadellidae of 30 species and 205 Delphacidae of 9 species. D. maidis accounted for n=3994, 90.1% of all leafhoppers and planthoppers, present in 64.1% of samples.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Sampling predates the 2015 onward corn stunt escalation. Sweep net samples adults preferentially. No per-municipality breakdown recovered from the extracted text.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: 48 municipalities, 8 states, 4 regions of Brazil, incl. 17 Parana municipalities
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Parana municipalities were directly sampled, so the dominance finding applies to the project geography

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Seventeen Parana localities in commercial maize crops were sampled, giving state-wide geographic coverage across west, north, centre and south Parana.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Sampling was 2005-2007 and single-visit per locality. The paper does not report a species list per municipality in the text recovered.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Parana: Lapa, Sao Mateus do Sul, Capanema, Cornelio Procopio, Campo Mourao, Toledo, Cafelandia, Santa Tereza do Oeste, Santo Antonio do Sudoeste, Cambe, Barracao, Santa Mariana, Mandaguari, Juranda, Maringa, Apucarana, plus the Toledo experimental station
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: This is the strongest direct Parana sampling frame located for maize-associated Auchenorrhyncha

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Collected in maize crops in Parana among four states; n=22, the 8th most abundant species overall and within the top ten that accounted for 97.6% of all specimens.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Co-occurs with D. maidis in maize crops; vector of Tomato curly top virus per Coelho et al. 2001
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: n=22 is a low absolute count. The source reports presence per state but not per municipality, and does not report life stage or whether maize is a reproductive host.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Goias, Parana, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Direct Parana record in commercial maize; the strongest non-target Cicadellidae evidence for the project geography

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Collected in maize crops in Parana among four states, and named among the eight species in the study recorded as vectors or potential vectors of maize viruses or mollicutes.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Co-occurs with D. maidis in maize; reported as an experimental vector of Spiroplasma kunkelii in maize in Argentina per Carloni et al.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: The S. kunkelii vector competence is experimental and from Argentina, not field-demonstrated in Brazil. Abundance for this species was not recovered from the extracted text.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Minas Gerais, Parana, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Direct Parana record in maize, and it is a Deltocephalinae like Dalbulus, so it is the closest-ranked non-target leafhopper with confirmed Parana presence

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Recorded in Parana among five states; n=36, 6th most abundant species. First record for Brazil in this study.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Co-occurs in maize; experimentally capable of transmitting Mal de Rio Cuarto virus to maize per Velazquez et al. 2006
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Vector competence is experimental only. MRCV is a quarantine virus in Brazil, not established. Delphacidae, so phylogenetically more distant from Dalbulus than Cicadellidae.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Maranhao, Piaui, Goias, Minas Gerais, Parana
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Pyrophagus tigrinus Remes Lenicov and Varela (Delphacidae)
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Direct Parana record in maize, but the organism is a planthopper not a leafhopper

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Recorded in Parana among five states; n=74, the second most abundant species overall after D. maidis. However 78.4% of specimens came from Maranhao and Piaui, so the authors judge it most common in the northeast.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Co-occurs in maize; experimentally transmitted Maize sterile stunt per Greber 1982
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: The authors explicitly attribute its abundance to the northeast, so the Parana contribution is small and unquantified in the recovered text.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Maranhao, Piaui, Goias, Minas Gerais, Parana
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Present in Parana but the source itself warns the species is a northeastern element

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Dalbulus maidis is the only species of the genus Dalbulus appearing in the study species list, across 4233 Cicadellidae specimens from 48 municipalities including 17 in Parana. The Brazilian literature reviewed identifies D. maidis as the only reported representative of the genus.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: This is absence of detection in one survey, not demonstrated absence from Brazil. Sweep netting may under-sample rare congeners. The study is from 2005-2007.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: No congeneric non-target leafhopper was detected in the project geography. Under D.5 the CLOSE_NON_TARGET_CICADELLIDAE category accepts phylogenetic_context in {SAME_GENUS, SAME_FAMILY}, so this is a phylogenetic coverage limitation and NOT a blocker for closing that category

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: 27 Cicadellidae species were identified in the centre-south states, 18 of them exclusive to that region. Jaccard similarity between centre-south and northeast was 0.30 for Cicadellidae, indicating markedly different faunas.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Region-level, not state-level. The identity of all 27 centre-south species is in a table that the text extraction rendered only partially.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Centre-south states: Goias, Minas Gerais, Sao Paulo, Parana, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Establishes that the Parana-relevant leafhopper community is distinct from the northeastern one, so northeastern records should not be transferred

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Named as one of only two species, with D. maidis, previously reported and widely known as vectors of mollicutes or viruses in Brazilian maize, and one of the eight vector or potential-vector species in the study.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Co-occurs in maize; long-known vector of maize mollicutes and viruses in Brazil alongside D. maidis
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: The per-state attribution for P. maidis was not recovered from the extracted text, so Parana presence is not established by this row.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Brazil, states for this species not recovered
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Brazilian maize association is established; Parana presence is UNRESOLVED and must not be assumed

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Among the ten most abundant species, which together accounted for 97.6% of all specimens: R. limbatula n=53, P. flavicosta n=41, B. incisa n=32, A. declivatus n=15.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Co-occur with D. maidis in Brazilian maize; P. flavicosta is among the eight vector or potential-vector species
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Per-state attribution not recovered for these four, so none can be assigned to Parana from this row. A. declivatus was a first record for Brazil.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Brazil, states for these species not recovered
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Rotigonalia limbatula (Osborn), Planicephalus flavicosta (Stal), Balclutha incisa (Matsumura), Atanus declivatus Linnavuori
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Brazilian maize association established; Parana presence UNRESOLVED for each

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM et al. 2013. Florida Entomologist 96(4):1470-1481.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: The genus Protalebrella appears in the study species table for Brazilian maize crops.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Present in the Brazilian maize leafhopper assemblage
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Identified only to genus in the recovered text, with no count and no state attribution.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Confirms the genus occurs in Brazilian maize but supports no Parana or species-level claim

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Bortolotto OC, Santos JVC, Ochonski AG. 2024. First report of earwig Doru luteipes (Dermaptera: Forficulidae) preying on corn leafhopper Dalbulus maidis (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) nymphs. Brazilian Journal of Biology 84.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Adults were hand-collected from the whorl region of plants in a commercial maize field with no insecticide applications, 50 days after planting, on 8 February 2024.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Generalist predator resident in the maize whorl
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: A single field, a single collection date, and no abundance or density data. The field was insecticide-free, which is not typical of commercial Parana maize.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Direct Parana field occurrence in commercial maize, at a known safrinha vegetative stage

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Bortolotto OC, Santos JVC, Ochonski AG. 2024. Brazilian Journal of Biology 84.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: In Petri-dish assays with one adult female and ten fourth-instar D. maidis nymphs over ten replicates, each adult consumed about 4.6 nymphs within 12 hours. The authors describe this as the initial evidence of earwigs preying on D. maidis nymphs.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Direct trophic link: D. luteipes consumes D. maidis nymphs
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Laboratory arena assay, not field predation. Ten replicates, one predator sex and stage, one prey instar, no-choice design. The authors state further research is required.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Laboratory, material sourced from Ponta Grossa, Parana
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Doru luteipes preying on Dalbulus maidis
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: The trophic link itself is demonstrated only in the laboratory; it must not be reported as a demonstrated field interaction in Parana

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Bortolotto OC, Santos JVC, Ochonski AG. 2024. Brazilian Journal of Biology 84.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: The authors state that D. maidis nymphs are mostly found in the whorl or on expanded leaves, the same plant region from which the earwigs were collected.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Explicitly attributed by the authors to personal observation, not to a measurement or a cited study.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Supports spatial co-occurrence of predator and prey in Parana maize, but only at the strength of an author observation

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Malerbo-Souza DT. 2011. The corn pollen as a food source for honeybees. Acta Scientiarum Agronomy 33(4).
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Africanized honey bees collected only pollen, and only from the male flowers (tassels), removing it with mouthparts and legs and packing it into pollen baskets. A. mellifera was 97.13% of insects observed in 2009 and 94.66% in 2010, and was classed as a constant species.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Sao Paulo, not Parana. Single site, single hybrid (DOW 2d587), three observation days per year, ten minutes per hour. 2009 and 2010 data only.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.resource_or_sugar_use: POLLEN_USE; no nectar collection recorded on maize
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Establishes the pollen-foraging pathway on Brazilian maize; Parana occurrence of the pathway is INFERRED, not demonstrated by this source

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Malerbo-Souza DT. 2011. Acta Scientiarum Agronomy 33(4).
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Trigona spinipes represented 4.23% of insects observed in 2010, collecting pollen from the tassels mainly between about 12:00 and 17:00, peaking about 14:00 to 16:00.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Sao Paulo, not Parana. Low relative frequency, recorded in one of two years, single site and hybrid.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: The only non-Apis bee with maize pollen collection directly verified in this review; Parana occurrence rests on a separate unreviewed source

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Malerbo-Souza DT. 2011. Acta Scientiarum Agronomy 33(4).
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Tetragonisca angustula represented 0.20% of insects observed in 2009, and an unidentified Trigona sp. was also recorded, both collecting pollen from tassels.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Sao Paulo, not Parana. 0.20% is a very low frequency from a single year and site; one taxon identified only to genus.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Weakest of the three bee records; supports the category but not a species-level panel entry

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Malerbo-Souza DT. 2011. Acta Scientiarum Agronomy 33(4).
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: The paper states that maize is characterised by anemophilous pollination, and notes that wind-pollinated plants can nonetheless benefit from insect visitors.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: A background statement within an agronomy paper rather than a primary pollination-biology study.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: General botanical statement in a Brazilian study
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Bears on exposure framing: bee presence at maize is driven by pollen as a resource, not by a pollination mutualism

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Malerbo-Souza DT. 2011. Acta Scientiarum Agronomy 33(4).
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Across both years and all bee taxa observed, collection was of pollen only; the paper reports no nectar foraging on maize.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Absence of report in one two-year single-site study is not demonstrated absence of the behaviour.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Apis mellifera and non-Apis bees on maize
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.resource_or_sugar_use: No nectar collection from maize was reported
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Constrains the plausible exposure route for bees to pollen and surface contact, not nectar ingestion

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Moya-Raygoza G. 2026. Biological control and management of Dalbulus maidis (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) with egg parasitoids: a review. Journal of Insect Science 26(2):ieag036.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Named as the main and most abundant egg parasitoids of D. maidis in maize fields across tropical America. A. virlai is described as the most abundant egg parasitoid in South American maize, citing Argentine studies. No Brazilian record and no Brazilian state is given anywhere in the reviewed text.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: The reference list was truncated in the retrieved text, so Brazilian records in the omitted portion cannot be ruled out. The only southern-Brazil citation visible concerns D. maidis abundance in Santa Catarina, not parasitoids. IMPORTANT: absence of a Brazilian record in THIS source is not absence of Brazilian evidence - see E-039, E-040 and E-041, which are Brazilian primary records.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Tropical America; Mexico and Argentina for the specific records
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Genus and species association with D. maidis is established for tropical America, but this source provides no Brazil and no Parana support

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Moya-Raygoza G. 2026. Journal of Insect Science 26(2):ieag036.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Six Dryinidae species are reported in the Americas as nymph and adult parasitoids of D. maidis. G. bartletti is the best studied and reached 24% parasitism in Mexican maize fields.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Nymph and adult parasitoid of D. maidis; the dryinid also preys on the vector
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: No Brazilian locality is given for any dryinid. The 24% figure is Mexican.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Establishes a second parasitoid guild that the current candidate list does not represent at all; no Parana support

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Moya-Raygoza G. 2026. Journal of Insect Science 26(2):ieag036.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Three Pipunculidae (Diptera) species and one Halictophagidae (Strepsiptera) species are reported in the Americas as parasitoids of D. maidis.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Nymph and adult parasitoids of D. maidis
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: No Brazilian localities. Identified at family level with species counts only.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Two further unrepresented guilds; no Parana or Brazil support from this source

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Moya-Raygoza G. 2026. Journal of Insect Science 26(2):ieag036, citing Casuso et al. 2025.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: About 40 arthropod predator species of D. maidis are reported across the Americas, spanning Araneae, Dermaptera, Hemiptera, Coleoptera, Neuroptera, Diptera and Hymenoptera.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Reported as a total across the Americas without a species list in the retrieved text. The primary source is Argentine and was not opened.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Americas; the cited primary study is from northern Argentina
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Arthropod predator assemblage of D. maidis
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Confirms the predator guild is taxonomically broad, which supports the PREDATOR category; it names no Brazilian or Parana species

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Moya-Raygoza G. 2024. Temporal resource continuity for egg parasitoids of Dalbulus maidis during winter on irrigated maize crops and edge grasses. Journal of Insect Science 24(4):14.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: All three taxa were recovered from asynchronously planted maize in 2022, with P. subflava most abundant and parasitism up to 53%. In 2023 only P. subflava was recovered, with under 2% parasitism on edge grasses.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Egg parasitoids of D. maidis on sentinel maize
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Mexico, high elevation, one site, one maize landrace, short sampling windows, Pseudoligosita identified only to genus. This study is frequently mis-attributed to Brazil in secondary summaries; it is not Brazilian.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Zapopan, Jalisco, Mexico, 20 deg 44 min N, 1662 m
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Anagrus virlai, Paracentrobia subflava, Pseudoligosita sp.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Not transferable to Parana. Recorded here because it is the source most often cited as Brazilian evidence for this parasitoid complex, and it is not

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Goncalves SL, Caramori PH, Wrege MS, Shioga P, Gerage AC. 2008. Epocas de semeadura do milho safrinha no Estado do Parana com menores riscos climaticos. Acta Scientiarum Agronomy 24:1287-1290.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Eight climatically homogeneous regions were identified within Parana, with safrinha sowing periods ranging from January to March across the state.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Only the abstract and metadata were read; the full PDF was not opened, so per-region dates were not obtained. The study is from 2008 and predates current cultivars and the Antecipe sowing practice.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Direct Parana crop-calendar evidence, but at state resolution only and not current

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Goncalves SL et al. 2008. Acta Scientiarum Agronomy 24:1287-1290.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Frost risk in the 30 days preceding maturity was the most restrictive factor for safrinha maize in Parana; water deficit was assessed at crop establishment and at flowering.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Abstract only. No calendar dates for flowering are given.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Constrains the late end of the Parana safrinha window, which bounds how late any receptor could co-occur with a standing crop

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM, Lopes JRS. 2000. Parasitoides de ovos da cigarrinha-do-milho, Dalbulus maidis (DeLong and Wolcott), em Piracicaba. Revista de Agricultura 75(2):263-270.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Reported via secondary summaries as identifying two egg parasitoid species of D. maidis over four consecutive maize plantings at Piracicaba.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Not opened. Secondary summaries disagree about the publication year (2000 versus 2015) for the same volume and issue, which must be resolved before citation. Sao Paulo, not Parana.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Anagrus breviphragma Soyka (Mymaridae) and Oligosita sp. (Trichogrammatidae)
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Would be the oldest Brazilian egg-parasitoid record, but from Sao Paulo and currently unverified

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Querino RB, Meneses AR, Luft Albarracin E, Oliveira CM, Triapitsyn SV. 2017. Biological control of Dalbulus maidis in Brazil: an overview of the parasitoids. In: Diseases in maize: insect vectors, mollicutes and viruses. Embrapa, p.121-140.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Reported via secondary summaries as the principal Brazilian synthesis, stating that Mymaridae and Trichogrammatidae are the main egg parasitoids and that P. subflava attacks D. maidis eggs in Brazilian maize cultivars.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Parasitoids of D. maidis in Brazil
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Not opened; only the abstract and secondary summaries were seen. The Brazilian localities cited by others are MG, SP and PI. No Parana record is reported by any summary consulted.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Brazil, with records cited for Sete Lagoas MG, Piracicaba SP and Teresina PI
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Mymaridae, Trichogrammatidae and Chalcidoidea parasitoids incl. Paracentrobia subflava
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: This is the single most important source still to retrieve for the PARASITOID category; until opened, no parasitoid can rest on reviewed Brazilian evidence

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Oliveira CM, Frizzas MR. 2021. Eight decades of Dalbulus maidis (DeLong and Wolcott) (Hemiptera, Cicadellidae) in Brazil: what we know and what we need to know. Neotropical Entomology 50:1-16.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Forum review of the species in Brazil since its 1938 first record, covering pest status, host plants, off-season survival strategies and management. Content on natural enemies was not retrievable.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Paywalled; the full text could not be opened. All content above comes from the abstract and from secondary summaries.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Likely the single best synthesis for Brazilian occurrence windows and off-season survival, and it remains unread

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Adapar and IDR-Parana statements reported in Agencia de Noticias do Parana and sector press, 2020-2025.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Reported that the leafhopper is present throughout Parana, and that of 64 samples collected across regions in November 2020, 40% carried pale and red stunt pathogens.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Institutional press material, not a peer-reviewed study. Not opened directly. Sampling design, detection method and species identification are not described.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Would be direct Parana state-wide occurrence evidence if verified; currently it is press reporting of an agency statement

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Embrapa Milho e Sorgo. Flutuacao populacional de Dalbulus maidis em milho, safrinha 2022.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Yellow sticky traps in three areas from March to June 2022 recorded a population peak at maize stage V8 (162 adults on 25 April) in one trap and at V7 (16 May) in another, with no correlation found to phenological stage, temperature or precipitation.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Not opened. Minas Gerais, not Parana. Single season, three areas. The authors themselves report no correlation with phenology, which weakens any phenological generalisation.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Indicates an early-vegetative peak in safrinha maize, but in MG; transfer to Parana is an inference

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Projeto Alerta Cigarrinha, Marechal Candido Rondon, safrinha 2023, reported in sector press.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: 68 traps were installed before safrinha sowing and changed weekly to the reproductive stage; a dilution effect was observed as insects concentrated near summer maize then dispersed into the larger safrinha area.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Sector press reporting a monitoring programme, not a peer-reviewed study. Not opened. No numeric series available.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Directly relevant Parana migration dynamic between the two crops, but at press-report strength only

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Survey of predatory Coccinellidae in vegetable crops, Campos Gerais region, in collaboration with Universidade Federal do Parana.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: 318 coccinellid individuals of eleven predatory species were recorded, including C. sanguinea, E. connexa and H. axyridis, with the invasive H. axyridis noted as predominant over native species.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Not opened. The crop system is vegetables, not maize. Conference proceedings rather than a journal article. No link to D. maidis.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Cycloneda sanguinea, Eriopis connexa, Harmonia axyridis and eight further predatory species
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Establishes that these three species occur in Parana agroecosystems, but not that they occur in Parana maize or interact with D. maidis

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Survey of predators in second-crop maize, Ribeirao Preto region, reported in Embrapa and academic material.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Reported that Doru spp., Geocoris spp., Orius sp. and Coccinellidae are the most common predators in second-crop maize, with Orius predominating in the late vegetative stage and during grain formation and ripening.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Not opened. Sao Paulo, not Parana. Identification mostly to genus. The relative abundance figures reported in secondary summaries were ambiguous as to which taxon they describe.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Doru spp., Geocoris spp., Orius sp., Coccinellidae
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Supports the PREDATOR category for Brazilian second-crop maize at genus level; supplies no Parana and no species-level entry

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Embrapa statements on natural enemy migration into second-crop systems.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Reported that with the harvest of summer crops, natural enemies abundant at the end of the cycle, such as chrysopids, migrate and concentrate in second-crop fields.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Generalist predators of aphids and soft-bodied prey
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Not opened. Goias and Minas Gerais. A qualitative statement in technical material rather than a quantified study.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.resource_or_sugar_use: Adults feed on nectar, pollen and aphid exudates per Embrapa technical material
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: If verified, it would mean the predator guild is concentrated in exactly the safrinha window where D. maidis peaks; currently unverified and not Parana

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Secondary summaries of Dalbulus elimatus distribution studies in Mexico, and of Brazilian Dalbulus surveys.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: D. elimatus is reported from seven Mexican states between 771 and 2050 m elevation, on maize and on evergreen grasses around maize fields. Secondary summaries of Brazilian surveys state that D. maidis is the only Dalbulus species recorded on maize in Brazil.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Congener of D. maidis on maize and edge grasses
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Not opened. The Brazilian no-congener statement is corroborated independently by E-007, which was opened and reviewed.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Mexico: Guanajuato, Hidalgo, Jalisco, Michoacan, Oaxaca, Puebla, Zacatecas
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: No evidence places D. elimatus in Brazil, let alone Parana. It cannot be justified as an ecological receptor for this geography on current evidence

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Study of Tetragonisca angustula subspecies and Trigona spinipes using nests from the Tibagi river basin, maintained at the Universidade Estadual de Londrina meliponary.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Nests of both taxa were collected in the Tibagi basin in Parana and maintained at a Londrina meliponary, for a study of respiratory rate.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Not opened. The study subject is respiratory physiology, not foraging or crop association. Nest provenance implies occurrence but the paper is not an occurrence survey.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Would supply the Parana occurrence leg for Trigona spinipes, whose maize-pollen use is demonstrated only in Sao Paulo; it must be opened before that chain is relied on

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Embrapa Trigo and Embrapa Milho e Sorgo technical communications on Rhopalosiphum maidis.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Reported as occurring in practically all regions of Brazil and causing economic damage to maize, with high infestations surprising southern producers in the 2005/2006 season.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Maize phloem feeder, co-occurs with D. maidis, transmits maize mosaic
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Not opened. Technical communications rather than peer-reviewed surveys, and from 2006. No Parana-specific survey was located.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Brazil, with outbreak reports for the South region in 2005-2006
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Southern Brazil association is reported; a Parana maize occurrence record at species level was not located in this review
