10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Santana DLQ, Waquil JM, Oliveira E. 1997. Ocorrencia de Anagrus breviphragma Soyka (Hymenoptera: Mymaridae) parasitando ovos de Dalbulus maidis no Brasil. In: Congresso Brasileiro de Entomologia, 16, and Encontro Nacional de Fitossanitaristas, 7, Salvador. Resumos. Salvador: SEB/EMBRAPA-CNPMF, p.101.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Primary Brazilian record of A. breviphragma parasitising eggs of D. maidis, titled explicitly as an occurrence in Brazil. This is the earliest Brazilian parasitoid record located for the target species.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Conference abstract from 1997; only the Embrapa catalogue record was retrievable, not the abstract text. The study locality and Brazilian state are not stated in the record, so the finding supports Brazil but no region.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Brazil, study locality not stated in the record (Salvador is the congress venue)
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Establishes Brazilian occurrence of a D. maidis egg parasitoid, but with no locality it supports no regional claim and specifically no Parana claim

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Meneses AR, Silva RBQ da, Olmi M, Oliveira CM de, Silva PRR, Bezerra VS. 2013. Descoberta de Gonatopus flavipes (Olmi) como um novo parasitoide de Dalbulus maidis (DeLong & Wolcott). Resumo em anais e proceedings. Embrapa Meio-Norte.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Records the discovery of G. flavipes as a new parasitoid of D. maidis in maize in Brazil, from weekly visits to Embrapa Meio-Norte maize plantings in Teresina, Piaui, in October 2012.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Recorded as a new parasitoid of D. maidis in maize in Brazil. Dryinidae specialise on Auchenorrhyncha, chiefly Cicadellidae, Delphacidae and Membracidae.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Conference abstract; no parasitism rate, no sample size and no host life stage are given. One month of observation at one experimental site. The abstract does not claim a worldwide first record, only a new record for D. maidis in Brazil.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Maize plantings at the Embrapa Meio-Norte experimental area, Teresina, Piaui, Brazil; weekly visits during October 2012
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Brazilian record in maize, from Piaui. It establishes that the nymph and adult parasitoid guild (Dryinidae) is present in Brazilian maize, which the earlier draft wrongly described as an entirely unrepresented guild. No Parana support.

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Meneses AR, Silva NNP da, Querino RB, Oliveira CM. 2015. Ocorrencia e flutuacao populacional de parasitoides de Dalbulus maidis (DeLong & Wolcott) (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) em milho. In: 14 Simposio de Controle Biologico (SICONBIOL), 14-18 June 2015, Teresopolis, RJ. Londrina: Sociedade Entomologica do Brasil.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Weekly collections using sentinel plants bearing D. maidis eggs on their leaves identified three species: A. breviphragma, P. subflava and P. longifrangiata. The authors state these are the FIRST RECORDS of P. subflava and P. longifrangiata parasitising D. maidis eggs in Brazil, and the first record of the A. breviphragma association with the corn leafhopper in the Brazilian Northeast.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.host_or_prey_relationship: Egg parasitoids attacking D. maidis eggs on sentinel plants
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Conference abstract, so no parasitism rates, no replication detail, no identification keys and no statistical treatment are reported. One experimental site in Piaui over 15 months. Species identifications are not independently verifiable from the abstract. The PDF renders the genus as Paracentobia, a typographic error for Paracentrobia.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Maize crops in the Embrapa Meio-Norte experimental area, Teresina, Piaui, Brazil; February 2013 to May 2014
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Anagrus breviphragma Soyka (Mymaridae), Paracentrobia subflava (Girault) and Pseudoligosita longifrangiata (Viggiani) (Trichogrammatidae)
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: This is the decisive Brazilian evidence for the PARASITOID category: three species, at species level, with explicit first-record claims. It is Piaui, in the Northeast, so it supports Brazil and not Parana. E-008 showed the centre-south and northeast leafhopper faunas differ markedly, which is a reason not to transfer the parasitoid assemblage to Parana without a regional record.

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Meneses AR, Silva NNP da, Querino RB, Oliveira CM. 2015. SICONBIOL 14, Teresopolis.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: The parasitoids occurred predominantly during the rainy season. Increases in the rainfall index were followed by increases above the mean number of parasitoids collected, and the highest rainfall index coincided with the parasitoid population peak.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: Conference abstract with no numeric series, no correlation statistics and no effect sizes. Piaui has a markedly different rainfall regime from Parana, so the calendar months of the rainy season do not transfer.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.location: Teresina, Piaui, Brazil; February 2013 to May 2014
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.organism: Egg parasitoid assemblage of D. maidis
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Supplies a NATURAL_ENEMY_WINDOW signal keyed to rainfall rather than to calendar date, which is the transferable part. The Piaui calendar itself is not transferable to Parana.

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: Study of Apis mellifera colonies at Mandirituba, Parana, in Archives of Veterinary Science / Revista do Setor de Ciencias Agrarias, UFPR. Citation supplied by the project reviewer.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Cited by the project reviewer as Parana literature involving A. mellifera colonies at Mandirituba, supporting occurrence of the species in the project geography.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: The URL timed out twice from this environment and the source was not retrieved, so neither the citation details nor the finding were verified here. The study concerns colonies at a locality and is not reported to concern maize.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: If verified, supplies the Parana OCCURRENCE leg for A. mellifera, which combines with the Sao Paulo maize-foraging leg (E-015). Occurrence in Parana does not demonstrate maize use in Parana.

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: UFPR digital repository item recording Trigona spinipes nests at Pinhais, Parana. Citation supplied by the project reviewer.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Cited by the project reviewer as recording T. spinipes nests at Pinhais, Parana, supporting occurrence of the species in the project geography.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: The host refused the connection from this environment and the source was not retrieved, so nothing was verified here. The reviewer states explicitly that this does not demonstrate maize use in Parana.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: If verified, supplies the Parana OCCURRENCE leg for T. spinipes, which combines with the Sao Paulo maize pollen-use leg (E-016). It supersedes E-037 as the occurrence source and does not establish maize use in Parana.

10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.citation: SciELO Arquivos do Instituto Biologico / Anais da Sociedade Entomologica do Brasil article describing D. maidis as the only reported representative of the genus in Brazil. Citation supplied by the project reviewer.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.finding: Cited by the project reviewer as Brazilian literature describing D. maidis as the only reported representative of the genus Dalbulus in Brazil, with a 2017 synthesis reporting that only D. maidis appeared among thousands of individuals sampled across Brazilian localities.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.limitations: The server returned HTTP 504 from this environment and the source was not retrieved. The 2017 synthesis referred to is E-028, also unopened.
10_l1_l2_l3_l8_ecological_evidence_v2.ts.transferability_to_project_geography: Independently corroborates E-007, which WAS opened and read. Two independent lines now support the same scoped statement, which is why the phrasing used is the only reported representative rather than an absolute absence claim.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DEFINITIONAL. Zea mays is the crop system named in REFERENCE_USE_GEOGRAPHY.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: DIRECT_PARANA. Commercial maize in 17 Parana municipalities is the sampling frame of E-002, and commercial maize in Ponta Grossa is the field in E-012.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: The treated plant itself. Any application route under the exposure envelope places product on or in this receptor, so no scenario removes it. Maize is anemophilous, so the plant is a pollen source rather than a pollination mutualist, which shapes the pollinator pathway rather than the plant pathway.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Separate decision track required per C-8: plant uptake and RNAi competence differ from arthropods, so no shared trigger set or disposition rationale.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED. Eighth most abundant species in a 48-municipality Brazilian maize survey, within the top ten that comprised 97.6% of specimens.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: DIRECT_PARANA. Collected in maize crops in Parana among four states (Goias, Parana, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul), n=22.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: A non-target Cicadellidae with a verified Parana record in commercial maize, phytophagous on the treated plant, and itself a virus vector (Tomato curly top virus). It occupies the same feeding guild and the same plant as the target without being the target. D.5 admits this category at phylogenetic_context in {SAME_GENUS, SAME_FAMILY}, so SAME_FAMILY is sufficient for closure.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: n=22 across four states is a low absolute count, and the source reports neither life stage nor whether maize is a reproductive host rather than an incidental one. Sampling was 2005-2007.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED. Named among the eight species in the survey recorded as vectors or potential vectors of maize viruses or mollicutes.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: DIRECT_PARANA. Collected in maize in Minas Gerais, Parana, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: NOT IN THE CURRENT PLAN LIST. A Deltocephalinae leafhopper, the same subfamily as Dalbulus, with a verified Parana record in maize, and an experimental vector of the same pathogen (Spiroplasma kunkelii) that the target transmits. On the evidence reviewed it is the closest-ranked non-target leafhopper with confirmed Parana presence, and it closes the category at SAME_FAMILY under D.5.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Vector competence for S. kunkelii is experimental and Argentine, not field-demonstrated in Brazil. Abundance was not recovered from the extracted text, so its commonness in Parana is unquantified.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED. Resident in the maize whorl in a Parana commercial field.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: DIRECT_PARANA. Adults hand-collected from the whorl of a commercial insecticide-free maize field in Ponta Grossa, Parana, 50 days after planting, 8 February 2024.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: The best-evidenced receptor in this review and the only candidate with both a Parana field occurrence in commercial maize and a demonstrated trophic link to the target: adult females consumed about 4.6 fourth-instar D. maidis nymphs per 12 hours. Predator and prey are both reported from the same plant region (whorl), so co-location on maize supports a plausible exposure pathway under compatible foliar scenarios. Under D.5 the PREDATOR category requires one receptor with a plausible trophic pathway, not species redundancy, so this receptor alone closes the category.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: The trophic link is demonstrated in a Petri-dish no-choice assay, not in the field; the authors state further research is required. One field, one date, no density data, and the field was insecticide-free, which is not typical of commercial Parana maize. No application route is assumed: PRODUCT_APPLICATION_WINDOW is UNRESOLVED, so the exposure pathway is stated as plausible under compatible scenarios and not as realised.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED in Sao Paulo. Africanized honey bees collected pollen, and only pollen, from maize tassels; 97.13% and 94.66% of insects observed in two years, classed as a constant species.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: DIRECT_PARANA, pending retrieval. A Parana study involving A. mellifera colonies at Mandirituba is supplied by the project reviewer (E-043) but could not be retrieved from this environment. Parana occurrence is therefore supported by a named Parana source rather than by inference alone.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: POLLINATOR is a mandatory category and this is the only pollinator with a directly reviewed, quantified foraging record on Brazilian maize. The pathway is specific and bounded: pollen collection at the tassel during anthesis, with no nectar foraging reported. The two legs are now a named Parana occurrence source and a reviewed Sao Paulo maize-use source.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification_status: LITERATURE_BACKED for maize use; Parana occurrence SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: The decision required is one of TRANSFERABILITY, not of evidence existence: is direct Parana occurrence plus direct maize use in another Brazilian state sufficient for CORE_PROPOSED? No Parana maize-foraging record was located for any bee. The maize-use evidence is one site, one hybrid, two years, ten minutes of observation per hour. The species is not native, so it does not represent native bees.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED in Sao Paulo. 4.23% of insects observed in 2010, collecting pollen from maize tassels, peaking about 14:00 to 16:00.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: DIRECT_PARANA, pending retrieval. Nests recorded at Pinhais, Parana, per a project-supplied UFPR repository item (E-044) that the host refused from this environment. This supersedes E-037 as the occurrence source.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: The only non-Apis bee whose maize pollen collection in Brazil was verified by direct source review in this work. It answers the plan's open non-Apis native bee slot with a named species rather than a category, and it now has a named Parana occurrence source.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification_status: LITERATURE_BACKED for maize use; Parana occurrence SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Same transferability decision as A. mellifera: the maize-use leg is Sao Paulo and reviewed, the Parana leg is a named source that was not retrieved. The reviewer notes explicitly that Parana occurrence does not demonstrate maize use in Parana.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED in Sao Paulo, but at 0.20% of insects observed in a single year.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING. Covered by the same unretrieved Parana sources as Trigona spinipes; no Pinhais record is claimed for this species.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: Adds a second non-Apis bee lineage to the pollinator track, with maize tassel pollen collection recorded in Brazil.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification_status: LITERATURE_BACKED for the maize association; Parana occurrence SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: 0.20% in one year at one site is near the detection floor. The record supports the category but is too thin to carry a CORE entry on its own.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED for tropical America, and the most abundant egg parasitoid in South American maize per Argentine studies. No Brazilian record located: the Anagrus recorded on D. maidis eggs in Brazil is A. breviphragma, not A. virlai.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED. No Parana record was found in any source consulted.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: Host relationship with D. maidis eggs is well established at continental scale. It is retained as a conditional candidate because the congeneric A. breviphragma is the species actually recorded in Brazil, which makes A. virlai a plausible but unrecorded addition rather than a justified receptor.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification_status: SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING for Brazil; LITERATURE_BACKED for tropical America
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: The 2026 review that was opened gives no Brazilian record for this species. The study most often cited as Brazilian evidence for this complex (E-024) is in fact from Jalisco, Mexico. Brazilian Anagrus records on D. maidis are for A. breviphragma (E-039, E-041), a different species.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED for Brazil. Identified on sentinel plants bearing D. maidis eggs in maize at Teresina, Piaui, Feb 2013 to May 2014, and stated by the authors to be the FIRST RECORD of the species parasitising D. maidis eggs in Brazil. Also named as one of the two main egg parasitoids across tropical America.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED. No Parana record was found in any source consulted. Recorded as PARASITOID_PARANA_COVERAGE_GAP.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: The best-documented parasitoid of the target in Brazil: species-level identification, an explicit Brazilian first record, a sentinel-plant method, and independent continental-scale support. It supplies the PARASITOID ecological function, which no other candidate covers, and the parasitoid pathway (PARASITOID_HOST_MEDIATED) that no other receptor carries.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: The Brazilian record is Piaui, in the Northeast, not Parana, and it is a conference abstract with no parasitism rates or replication detail. E-008 showed the centre-south and northeast leafhopper faunas differ markedly (Jaccard 0.30), which is a reason not to transfer the parasitoid assemblage to Parana without a regional record. The Parana gap is documented, not closed.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED for Brazil. Identified on sentinel plants bearing D. maidis eggs in maize at Teresina, Piaui, and stated by the authors to be the FIRST RECORD of the species parasitising D. maidis eggs in Brazil.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: A second Trichogrammatidae egg parasitoid of the target with a Brazilian species-level first record. It adds within-guild redundancy rather than a new ecological function, so EXTENDED rather than CORE.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Piaui, not Parana, and from a conference abstract. Same family as the CORE parasitoid candidate, so it adds no new phylogenetic coverage within the guild. The earlier draft recorded this genus as having no Brazilian record and as the least justified of the three parasitoid genera; that was wrong, and is corrected here.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED for Brazil. Recorded as a new parasitoid of D. maidis in maize at the Embrapa Meio-Norte experimental area, Teresina, Piaui, from weekly visits in October 2012. Six Dryinidae species parasitise D. maidis across the Americas, and G. bartletti reached 24% parasitism in Mexican maize.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: A Dryinidae attacking nymphs and adults rather than eggs, with a Brazilian maize record. It adds BOTH a new ecological function combination (parasitoid that also preys on the vector) and a new exposure pathway relative to the egg parasitoids, which under D.5 is an argument for CORE rather than EXTENDED. It is proposed as EXTENDED here only because the PARASITOID category is already closed by P. subflava, and the CORE question is flagged as an OPEN_DECISION rather than decided by this review.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Piaui, not Parana. Conference abstract with no parasitism rate, no sample size and no host life stage. One month of observation. The earlier draft described the nymph and adult parasitoid guild as entirely unrepresented in Brazil; that was wrong, and is corrected here.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING. Orius sp. is reported among the most common predators in second-crop maize in Sao Paulo, predominating in the late vegetative stage and during grain formation; Embrapa technical material names O. insidiosus among emphasised maize predators.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED at species level in Parana maize.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: A predatory Hemipteran, so it carries both PREDATOR function and SAME_ORDER phylogenetic proximity on two independent axes, which is the combination the plan's D.2 design is built for.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: The Brazilian maize evidence is at genus level and from Sao Paulo, in sources that were not opened. No Parana record and no species-level record in maize was located. No documented trophic link to D. maidis.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING. Named by Embrapa among emphasised maize predators; chrysopids are reported to migrate into second-crop fields after the summer harvest, in Goias and Minas Gerais.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED in Parana maize.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: Adults feed on nectar, pollen and aphid exudates, so the receptor has a resource-use pathway distinct from pure predation, which adds an exposure route the other predators do not supply.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: No source naming C. externa in Parana maize was located, and none of the supporting material was opened. The safrinha migration claim is qualitative technical material from other states. No documented trophic link to D. maidis.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED for Parana maize. Coccinellidae as a family are reported among common predators in Sao Paulo second-crop maize.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING. All three are recorded in the Campos Gerais region of Parana, but in vegetable crops, not maize, in an unopened conference paper.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: The plan asks for a regionally justified Coccinellidae. These three are the species with a located Parana agroecosystem record, but the record is from the wrong crop system. Conditional on a maize-system record being retrieved.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Presence in Parana vegetables does not establish presence in Parana maize, and no source links any of the three to D. maidis. H. axyridis is additionally an invasive species, which raises a separate question about whether an invasive predator should occupy a beneficial-receptor slot.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.organism: Coccinellidae: Cycloneda sanguinea, Eriopis connexa, Harmonia axyridis

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING. Reported as occurring in practically all regions of Brazil and causing economic damage to maize.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING. Outbreaks reported for the South region in 2005/2006; no Parana survey located.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: A non-target maize phloem feeder in the same order as the target, sharing the treated plant and the feeding mode, and a plausible prey item linking the herbivore and predator tracks.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Supporting material is Embrapa technical communications from around 2006, not opened, with no Parana survey. It is a pest rather than a beneficial, which does not reduce its value as a non-target but should be stated plainly.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED for Brazil. One of only two species, with D. maidis, previously reported and widely known as vectors of mollicutes or viruses in Brazilian maize.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: UNRESOLVED. The per-state attribution for this species was not recovered from the opened source.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: A Delphacid sharing the maize host, the phloem-feeding mode and the vector role with the target, which makes it a close functional analogue even though it is phylogenetically more distant than the Cicadellidae candidates.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification_status: LITERATURE_BACKED for Brazil; Parana presence UNRESOLVED
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Parana presence is specifically not established by the source that was opened, and must not be assumed from Brazilian presence.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED. Among the eight vector or potential-vector species in the survey; experimentally transmits Mal de Rio Cuarto virus.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: DIRECT_PARANA. Recorded in maize in Maranhao, Piaui, Goias, Minas Gerais and Parana; n=36, sixth most abundant species.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: A Delphacid with a verified Parana record in maize and a reasonable abundance, adding non-Cicadellidae Auchenorrhyncha coverage to the phylogenetic axis.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Vector competence is experimental only, for a virus that is a quarantine organism not established in Brazil. First record for Brazil in that 2013 study, so the occurrence history is short.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED. Second most abundant species overall, n=74.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: DIRECT_PARANA, but weak. Recorded in Parana among five states, while 78.4% of specimens came from Maranhao and Piaui.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: Second most abundant species in Brazilian maize overall, which would ordinarily argue for inclusion.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification_status: LITERATURE_BACKED for Brazil; Parana weight UNRESOLVED
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: The source itself states the species is most common in the northeast, so its national abundance rank overstates its Parana relevance. The Parana share is unquantified in the recovered text.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED for Brazil. Documented on maize and edge grasses in seven Mexican states between 771 and 2050 m.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED. No Brazilian record of any kind was located, let alone a Parana record.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: Cannot be justified as an ecological receptor for Parana: no exposure pathway exists for a species not present in the system. The Brazilian literature reviewed identifies D. maidis as the only reported representative of the genus, so no congeneric ecological receptor is available. This is a phylogenetic coverage limitation, NOT a blocker: D.5 admits CLOSE_NON_TARGET_CICADELLIDAE at SAME_GENUS or SAME_FAMILY, and the category is closed at SAME_FAMILY by Agallia albidula and Exitianus obscurinervis.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification_status: LITERATURE_BACKED for the exclusion; the Mexican distribution record is SOURCE_REVIEW_PENDING
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: This exclusion is ecological only. D. elimatus may still be proposed on the separate PHYLOGENETIC_PROXY axis, which D.4 keeps distinct from ecological receptor status, and that is a different decision that this review does not make. The absolute phrasing no congener is documented in Brazil is avoided: two independent sources (E-007 opened, E-045 reviewer-supplied) support the scoped statement only reported representative.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED for Brazil.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED. Not recorded in any Brazilian maize survey consulted.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: No ecological basis for inclusion in a Parana maize panel. Recorded explicitly so that the decision is on the record: this species is NOT proposed, and the quality of its sequence resources played no part in that or any other judgement in this table.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification_status: LITERATURE_BACKED for the absence of a Brazilian maize record in the survey reviewed
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Absence of detection in the surveys consulted is not demonstrated absence from Brazil. If it is later retained, it must be on the PHYLOGENETIC_PROXY axis, never as a Parana ecological receptor.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED for Brazil. An Asian rice leafhopper.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: No ecological basis for inclusion in a Parana maize panel, on the same grounds as H. vitripennis and with the same note: sequence resource quality played no part in this judgement.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification_status: LITERATURE_BACKED for the absence of a Brazilian maize record in the survey reviewed
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Same caveat: absence of detection is not demonstrated absence. Retention would have to be on the PHYLOGENETIC_PROXY axis only.

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: NOT_ASSESSED.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NOT_ASSESSED. No species is named, so no occurrence question can be posed.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: CONDITIONAL_PENDING_EXPOSURE_SCENARIO. The category cannot be populated because its exposure pathway is itself undecided: application route and formulation state are UNRESOLVED (N-3, N-4) and PRODUCT_APPLICATION_WINDOW is UNRESOLVED. Naming a species before the pathway exists would be inventing a receptor. The absence of a receptor becomes a true COVERAGE_GAP only if a frozen scenario assigns SOIL_OR_RESIDUE a plausibility of PLAUSIBLE or UNKNOWN.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: Parana maize is predominantly no-till with heavy surface residue, which would plausibly strengthen a residue pathway if a route were fixed, but no source was reviewed for this and it is recorded as an untested expectation, not a finding. Until a scenario is frozen this row is conditional, not a gap.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.organism: Soil or residue receptor, species unnamed

11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_maize_association: DIRECTLY_DEMONSTRATED for Brazil, by two independent records: a 1997 Embrapa record of the species parasitising D. maidis eggs in Brazil, and the 2015 Teresina sentinel-plant study, which also reports the first record of the association in the Brazilian Northeast.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.evidence_for_parana: NO_EVIDENCE_LOCATED. No Parana record was found in any source consulted.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.justification: The Brazilian Anagrus on D. maidis, and the longest-standing Brazilian parasitoid record for the target (1997 and 2015). As a Mymaridae it adds family-level phylogenetic coverage within the parasitoid guild that the Trichogrammatidae candidates do not supply.
11_nto_candidate_receptors_precontract_v.main_limitation: The 1997 record is a conference abstract whose study locality and state are not stated, and only its catalogue record was retrievable. The 2015 record is Piaui, not Parana, and also a conference abstract. No parasitism rates are available from either.

12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.coverage_gap: NONE at the category level. A within-category gap remains: no source was reviewed on dsRNA uptake or RNAi competence in maize, which belongs to the separate PLANT decision track under C-8.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.decision_needed: Confirm that the PLANT track carries its own trigger set and disposition rationale and shares none with the arthropod tracks.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.evidence_strength: STRONG_DIRECT_PARANA. The crop system is definitional to REFERENCE_USE_GEOGRAPHY, and commercial Parana maize is the sampling frame of two directly reviewed sources.

12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.coverage_gap: PHYLOGENETIC_COVERAGE_LIMITATION, not a category gap. D.5 admits this category at phylogenetic_context in {SAME_GENUS, SAME_FAMILY}, so SAME_FAMILY closes it. No congeneric receptor is available because the Brazilian literature reviewed identifies D. maidis as the only reported representative of the genus; that limitation is recorded and belongs to the separate PHYLOGENETIC_PROXY axis under D.4.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.decision_needed: Decide whether E. obscurinervis, which the plan does not list, is adopted. Decide separately whether a congeneric PHYLOGENETIC_PROXY is wanted on the D.4 axis, which is not a condition of closing this category.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.evidence_strength: STRONG_DIRECT_PARANA for both. Each has a verified record in Parana commercial maize in a 48-municipality survey that was opened and read, and each is a documented or experimental vector. E. obscurinervis is Deltocephalinae, the same subfamily as Dalbulus.

12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.coverage_gap: NO SPECIES GAP and no evidence-existence gap. The open item is a transferability rule, plus retrieval of two named Parana sources. No Parana maize-foraging record was located for any bee.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.decision_needed: Decide the transferability rule: is direct Parana occurrence plus direct maize use in another Brazilian state sufficient for CORE_PROPOSED? Retrieve E-043 and E-044 to confirm the occurrence leg. This is the only mandatory category whose closure turns on a methodological decision rather than on evidence.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.evidence_strength: MODERATE. Maize tassel pollen collection is directly demonstrated and quantified for both species, in Sao Paulo. Parana occurrence is supported by named Parana sources for both (Mandirituba for A. mellifera, Pinhais nests for T. spinipes), neither of which could be retrieved from this environment.

12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.candidate_receptor: Paracentrobia subflava (CORE_PROPOSED); Anagrus breviphragma, Pseudoligosita longifrangiata and Gonatopus flavipes (EXTENDED_PROPOSED)
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.coverage_gap: PARASITOID_PARANA_COVERAGE_GAP. Brazilian evidence is real and species-level; no Parana or southern-Brazil record was located in any source consulted. E-008 found the centre-south and northeast leafhopper faunas differ markedly (Jaccard 0.30), which is a reason not to transfer the Piaui parasitoid assemblage to Parana without a regional record. D.5 permits closing a mandatory category with an explicitly documented coverage gap, which is what is done here.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.decision_needed: Accept PARASITOID_PARANA_COVERAGE_GAP as the documented closure, or commission a directed Parana or southern-Brazil parasitoid search before the contract freezes. Decide separately whether G. flavipes should be CORE rather than EXTENDED, since as a nymph and adult parasitoid that also preys on the vector it adds both an ecological function and an exposure pathway that the egg parasitoids do not.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.evidence_strength: STRONG FOR BRAZIL, ABSENT FOR PARANA. Three egg parasitoid species were identified on sentinel plants bearing D. maidis eggs in maize at Teresina, Piaui (Feb 2013 to May 2014), with explicit first-record claims in Brazil for P. subflava and P. longifrangiata. A fourth species, the dryinid G. flavipes, was recorded as a new parasitoid of D. maidis in Brazilian maize at the same station in October 2012. A 1997 Embrapa record covers A. breviphragma in Brazil. All four sources are Brazilian primary records; three were opened and read.

12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.coverage_gap: NONE at the category level. D.5 requires one PREDATOR with a plausible trophic pathway, not species redundancy, so one strongly evidenced receptor closes the category. Orius insidiosus, Chrysoperla externa and the Coccinellidae remain EXTENDED_PROPOSED with their own gaps, and none of them blocks closure.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.decision_needed: No decision is required to close this category. Optional: decide whether to pursue a second, trophically independent predator as EXTENDED, and whether an invasive species (Harmonia axyridis) should occupy a beneficial-receptor slot.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.evidence_strength: STRONG_DIRECT_PARANA. The only candidate in this review with both a Parana field occurrence in commercial maize (Ponta Grossa, whorl, 50 days after planting, February 2024) and a demonstrated trophic link to the target (about 4.6 fourth-instar nymphs consumed per 12 hours). Both facts come from one directly reviewed source.

12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.coverage_gap: NOT YET A COVERAGE_GAP. The category is mandatory only conditional on the SOIL_OR_RESIDUE pathway being PLAUSIBLE or UNKNOWN, and that depends on application route and formulation state, which are UNRESOLVED (N-3, N-4), with PRODUCT_APPLICATION_WINDOW also UNRESOLVED. The absence of a receptor becomes a true COVERAGE_GAP only once a frozen scenario assigns the pathway PLAUSIBLE or UNKNOWN.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.decision_needed: Keep the category CONDITIONAL_PENDING_EXPOSURE_SCENARIO. Do not name a species. Revisit only when a route and formulation are fixed, or when the exposure envelope explicitly assigns the pathway PLAUSIBLE or UNKNOWN under a named scenario.
12_mandatory_category_closure_v2.tsv.evidence_strength: NOT_ASSESSABLE. The category's own trigger is undecided, so no occurrence question can be posed.
